title: Phyrexia: All Will Be One: card flavor text

paragraphs.text: There's never a need to change the watch, for the servants of Norn are sleepless.
"Be not afraid of the holy chorus. Join in rapturous harmony."
"Let those thanebound dissenters prattle about their dead god. I serve the Mother of Machines, and in her name I carve out their heresy."
"Elspeth, my friend, the Multiverse has answered my prayers to bring you here so that I may gather you into my pride and forever protect you."
"We need not be swift. We are inexorable."
"There is no hate behind our blades. We kill out of love, and the desire to share Norn's blessings with all."
"My mother wore this into battle against the first Phyrexians. Now I wear it in her honor."
"You think it's creepy now? You should see how it eats." —Melira
"I have room for a few more teeth in my collection. Who's next?"
"It's hard to fight for the future if you can't see the way forward."
While one mouth feeds, the other chatters mindless paeans of Elesh Norn's glory.
"Drown, so you may breathe again." —Atraxa
The mites sniff out any potential interlopers. He handles the rest.
Only Elesh Norn's most loyal servants are granted the honor of becoming part of her throne.
"Behold your inevitable defeat." —Elesh Norn
New Phyrexia's planar defenses scattered the Planeswalker strike team on arrival. Elesh Norn knew they were coming.
"Witness the glory of true, unwavering unity." —Ajani
"There is a single, glorious truth, etched in the hearts of the faithful. Join in unity, or be washed away."
"Well, aren't you a sight for sore eyes!" said Koth. "I was about to say the same, my friend," Elspeth replied.
He spreads word of the Argent Etchings to a captive audience.
"It's hard to tell with this glare, but those must be the skyhunter reinforcements! They have arrived at last!" —Prahan, Mirran rebel
Faced with a blast that would level not only New Phyrexia, but also a dozen innocent worlds, Elspeth consigned it—and herself—to the nothingness in between.
"Hear only harmony. See only glory. Speak only truth." —Atraxa
For the aspirants of the Progress Engine, being launched into the sphere's upper reaches is a great honor. Some are even granted wings beforehand.
It is Jin-Gitaxias's deepest exasperation that any part of his domain still requires maintenance.
"Where once there was ignorance, Jin-Gitaxias brought knowledge, and an age of progress dawned." —Monument inscription
Kaya watched in horror as the illusion vanished from her hands. Jace held the real Sylex—and had activated it before phyresis claimed his mind.
It can catch a rat and perform a spinal tap with one graceful swipe of its paw.
"Free will was an illusion so perfect it fooled even me. I know better now."
"Careful—however they might look, they're not human. A step too close and they'll drag you in." —Kara Vrist, resistance spymaster
One morning, the test subject decided to perform trials on the scientists.
"Drink deeply of the truth, and become *compleat*." —Tamiyo
An inconsistency in a routine vivisection sparked a revelation about the inner workings of the Orthodoxy's centurions.
Bored with the ruins of Lumengrid, it migrated to the ruins of the Mephidross.
"The oil is all-knowing. The trick is to ask the right questions."
"I've isolated the chirality of the glistening oil, so there will be no wasted precursors."
Each of the Gitaxian sectives watches the others, looking for any hint of imperfection.
"Imagine a giant room, like a library . . . except instead of books, it's filled with body parts." —Kara Vrist, resistance spymaster
No matter how many times he saw it, Sarnvax always relished the look of dawning horror as his foes realized their mistake.
"Please, for science, tell me how it feels. Leave nothing out."
It no longer needs to eat, but old instincts are put to use ridding the Surgical Bay of spies.
"Your theory holds merit. You do not." —Sarnvax, Gitaxian sective
"I bring a message from the Autonomous Furn—argh!"
Visitors to the Surgical Bay often become permanent residents.
"We are opening a new chapter in the one true story of Phyrexia. Someone must record it for posterity." —Tamiyo
"Experimental Log 290: Leaving the subject's pain receptors active appears to yield an unprecedented combination of incoherence and hyperawareness."
After a series of ambushes, Uulbrek demanded a sentry with no blind spots.
The Mirran forces thought they'd vanquished their foes . . . until a nearby monument got up and started stalking toward them.
By gaze, sting, and claw, Vraska will see the will of Phyrexia done.
Many vatkeepers use necrogen etchings to judge the value of their aspirants. If the wounds rot and fester, the recipient is not worth further effort.
"Watch your footing around here. Anything you might step on probably has teeth." —Kara Vrist, resistance spymaster
"Where once there was complacence, Sheoldred brought ambition, and soon the will of Yawgmoth reigned." —Monument inscription
"Get away from there! I must rebuild that one for the next bout. Shoo, shoo!" —Keskit, the Flesh Sculptor
What cannot be remade will be unmade, one scrap at a time.
The gospel of lies sounds sweetest when whispered by many mouths.
"We both serve the Demon Thane. Your parts would better serve with me."
Sinking into the Dross is neither a gentle death nor a quiet one. But once the necrogen takes hold, it is inevitable.
"Give of yourself, for compleation awaits the cleansed." —Nokar, priest of Sheoldred
They wished to become vital parts of the Dross Pits. Azax-Azog granted their request.
What she lacks in skin she makes up in swagger.
"It seems someone forgot to read the fine print."
"Does anyone else hear that horrible crunching sound?" —Jace
"I give you pain, you give me information. A simple trade, is it not?"
"Give all you are to Phyrexia, and you will receive more than you could have ever desired."
The praetors of the other Spheres privately wonder how Sheoldred always has a surplus of glistening oil at her disposal.
For a bittersweet moment, Jace believed he could still save his love. A moment was all Vraska needed. "For the glory of Phyrexia," she whispered.
"Show me what Norn's sycophants are hiding under all that pretty porcelain." —Sheoldred
Some of Sheoldred's goliaths spread the glory of Phyrexia. Others just eat.
"I have raised many of my own contenders for the Coliseum. This one will be fearsome one day, mark my words."
"Congratulations. I am entertained."
The punishment for sedition, like every other crime in the Dross Pits, is execution.
From within its form, a single word echoed forth: "Devour."
She proudly carries the weight of Phyrexia's creed, both figuratively and literally.
The first rebirth is a reward. The fifty-first is a punishment.
"Soon enough each praetor will have hired me to kill the others, and I will stand alone as the true Father of Machines."
The dull, creeping pain of phyresis curdled in Vraska's blood. She knew as soon as it took her, she would betray everything—even Jace.
"Live or die, you serve the Steel Thanes now."
The Invasion Tree broke through the Blind Eternities and sent Phyrexian perfection coursing across the Multiverse.
"Without faith in each other, we truly would have nothing left. Isn't that right, Malach? ...Malach?" —Darven, Mirran rebel, last words
"I will not rest until the truth of Phyrexia is inscribed across the Multiverse."
"Finally, a safe way to punch the rotters in the face."
"To dance to the music of Juex, leap like the flickering flame and hit like the hammer."
"They call themselves the Quiet Furnace? Ironic." —Tyvar
"They're violent, headstrong, and wildly unpredictable. It should be amusing to see how Norn's vaunted tactics try to cope with them." —Urabrask
He finally understood that phyresis was not an ending, but a new, perfect beginning.
She marks her favorite creations with a searing brand, leaving all others to be consumed by the furnace.
With the Quiet Furnace closed to all other factions, Urabrask's smiths were free to build anything their creativity demanded.
Urabrask encourages creativity in all its forms, even the destructive ones. Especially the destructive ones.
The Machine Orthodoxy finds strength in numbers. The Quiet Furnace finds that amusing.
"No matter how tough they are, even Phyrexians prefer to keep their guts on the inside." —Jor Kadeen
You would laugh too if you just burned through a tyrranax's stomach.
"Perhaps this will show the Orthodoxy what we think of their attempts at indoctrination."
Nahiri's last free breath became a defiant roar as she tore apart Sheoldred's Coliseum.
Popular wisdom says that Phyrexians don't feel fear. But popular wisdom has never tried to hold a bridge against an angry ogre.
"That Great Work of yours is looking pretty fragile, Urabrask!"
"Where once there was apathy, Urabrask brought passion, and the Great Work truly began." —Monument inscription
When the Vulshok taught him the word for "home," he knew it was what he had been fighting for.
Sometimes the Great Work requires destruction to allow for more efficient reconstruction.
"They may have unlimited mites, but that just means we have unlimited ammunition." —Urabrask
Once he fought to save Mirrodin. Now he fights to remake it.
As the infection spread, Nahiri's thoughts grew tangled. She needed to protect what she loved from Phyrexia... or maybe only Phyrexia could protect what she loved.
"You were so eager to spy on my work, I assume you'll appreciate a hands-on demonstration."
Her faith burns hot enough to sear away the flesh of the heretic.
"There's a war brewing between Norn and Urabrask. Exploit the chaos, and we can take them both down for good." —Koth
"Not my style, but it'll get the job done." —Nahiri
"Eat. Sort. Eat. Sort. Eat."
Some Vicious Swarm aspirants hang motionless in the canopy for weeks, allowing poisonous flowers to root in their flesh and weave tendrils through their hair.
Its webs are not true silk, but woven from thousands of delicate mycosynth strands.
Warm forges and tasty goblins lured it from the Hunter Maze to the Quiet Furnace.
"This one needs a bit longer to ripen." —Glissa Sunslayer
"Let me tell you why you must never close your eyes when on watch. Not even for a second." —Jor Kadeen
"Urabrask doesn't think big enough." —Glissa Sunslayer
Even as they brought the beast down, they could feel its poison working into their blood, altering their bodies, and filling their minds with the thrill of the eternal hunt.
Metal or flesh, it didn't matter—seasoned with ichor, it all tasted so good.
The strategies and politics of the Vicious Swarm are as subtle as Vorinclex himself.
"Best we move on. That gurgling means it's feeding time." —Melira
"All elves aspire to be part of nature. Only Phyrexia can truly grant that wish." —Glissa Sunslayer
In the Hunter Maze, today's apex predator is tomorrow's prey.
"I bet even Skithiryx would take the long way around this one." —Kara Vrist, resistance spymaster
"It is as the Mirrans say: True strength comes from within." —Ich-Tekik, Salvage Splicer
While some predators specialize in speed, size, or deadly venom, the adaptive tyrranax see no need to limit themselves.
"When they write songs about this battle, I will make sure your name is forgotten, devil."
"If you don't reassemble me immediately, the Mother of Machines will notice my absence, and this entire layer will face her wrath!"
"This was once a peaceful spring, but I wouldn't advise taking a sip." —Melira
Silent observers swim through the air of Norn's Seedcore, watching the nascent Invasion Tree for any signs of interference.
"Ah, my old friends. Have you decided at last to stop clinging to the past and join me in the grand pursuit of perfection?"
After giving in to the thrill of the hunt, he could never again return to the quiet of the Basilica.
"May you rejoice in the magnificence of Norn. May your flesh serve perfection."
It shines with the conviction of a zealous acolyte.
It seethes with the ambition of a ruthless gladiator.
The shifting, unpredictable sands were deemed a disobedient affront to the Flesh Singularity.
It burns with the passion of an unbound creator.
It pulses with the might of an apex predator.
"Melira helped me design it. Those who are infected by the oil cannot cross the threshold. We should be safe inside." —Koth
Humble, obedient, and tireless, myr require little modification to excel as servants of Phyrexia.
"Myr will go where the work is. We always have. We always will." —Urtet, Remnant of Memnarch
"Our resistance is like the myr: small and easily overlooked, but loyal and resilient beyond measure." —Melira
Since conquering Mirrodin, Phyrexian engineers have worked tirelessly to transform the plane's original two layers into a more fitting array of nine.
"The five suns may have dimmed, but their light still guides us." —Thrun
Why carry a subject to a surgical lab when you can bring the surgical lab to them?
"Lock the door and eat the key." —Vraan, Executioner Thane
It crackles with the intellect of a twisted genius.
It watches through the never-ending day, motionless save for the unsettling, twitching dance it performs as each sun reaches its apex.
In Urabrask's domain, mighty forges echo day and night with the clangor of the Great Work.
Where ambition meets industry, passion is poisoned by greed.
Where fire meets ferocity, a greater evolution begins.
Where curiosity meets cruelty, hideous innovations arise.
In Sheoldred's domain, the Steel Thanes wage a never-ending war in her long shadow.
In Elesh Norn's domain, the gospel of unity is the highest law.
In Vorinclex's domain, only the mightiest survive, and all are prey in his endless hunt.
As the Invasion Tree grew, its branches pierced through the world's silent core.
Where evolution meets austerity, primal might bucks against the yoke of hierarchy.
Where indoctrination meets inquiry, currents roil restlessly beneath the surface.
In Jin-Gitaxias's domain, strange and terrible experiments iterate toward perfection, unbound by ethics.
"The Phyrexian's monuments of today will be nothing but dust tomorrow. With enough tomorrows, so will their rule." —Koth
To resist the embrace of the Flesh Singularity is to reject unconditional acceptance.
Etch your victories in iron, that the world may celebrate them forever.
Be the blade that severs hierarchy.
Submit and know the Mother's glory. Resist and and know her wrath.
Take everything from them. Lives. Flesh. The very ground they walk on. Only then will your victory be compleat.
Do not fear death. Fear failure.
A thousand riddles, each with a single answer: "The glory of Phyrexia."
Never get between a goblin and the closest shiny object.
Obedience is the armor that turns any blade.
Phyrexia will stretch from sea to sky, across worlds and realities, inescapable and perfect.
Even the most insignificant creature can be perfected.
Take everything from them. Lives. Flesh. The very gorund they walk on. Only then will your victory be compleat.
The Forge embraces all who contribute to the Great Work.
Will you be the flame which burns the world, or merely be consumed as fuel?
Feel the joy of losing yourself to feed the land.
Who is an enemy but a friend who has yet to accept perfection?
In the embrace of the Mother of Machines, hard work never goes unrewarded.
